exposure: exposure to blood products (factor, bypassing agents)
outcome: patient demographics and characteristics of acquired hemophilia
outcomes of immune tolerance therapy (successful, unsuccessful, active treatment)
cohort: The study participants were 166 patients with acquired hemophilia (83 women, 73 men, median age 70 years) registered in the Hemostasis and Thrombosis Research Society (HTRS) Registry.
finding: The study found that acquired hemophilia patients in the US HTRS Registry were mostly non-Hispanic whites (61.4%) with a median age of 70 years, commonly presenting with autoimmune disease (28.4%) or malignancy (14.5%), and subcutaneous bleeding was the most common first site, particularly in white and non-Hispanic individuals.
